fix: Reword the shelf concern at turbotab/core/models/repeated.py:729-731 from 'fewer than the 8 a sandwich interval needs' to 'fewer than the 8 units TurboTab requires (a convention, the seal's unit floor)', matching floor_refusal at inference.py:263; add a binary-outcome GEE type-I test beside test_gee_type_one_error_at_twelve_units.
evidence: I ran the app's gee_table under the null. At 12 units it rejects 0.048 for a numeric outcome. With a rare binary outcome (about 4%) and 3 of 12 units exposed it rejects 0.016-0.029, so it is conservative, not liberal. That rejects Referee B's 0.123 for this implementation and supports Referee A. With the floor bypassed at 6 units it rejects 0.064, so the floor of 8 is a defensible conservative convention with no methods source (both referees and the audit agree). floor_refusal labels the floor as 'TurboTab requires', but the shelf text states it as what 'a sandwich interval needs'. The exits are task-correct: mixed model for a number, combining rows for yes/no. Aside: gee_working raises an uncaught ValueError when the estimated exchangeable alpha is negative enough for large units, e.g. ICC near 0 with 30-40 rows per unit.

fix: At turbotab/core/stages/modeling.py:2384-2385, pass spec.levers to imbalance_sentence (modeling.py:1079) and, when levers['imbalance'] != 'none', return a sentence naming the correction and its recalibration (or None, leaving levers.decision_sentence to say it), with a test that runs a binary fit with imbalance='weights'.
evidence: Both referees and the audit agree the default is sound (van den Goorbergh 2022; Referee B's weighting simulation extends it). The defect is in the code. imbalance_sentence is emitted unconditionally for every binary fit (modeling.py:2384), while pipeline.py:825-828 wraps the model in ImbalanceCorrected whenever the Explore lever (explore.py:596-612) sets weights, undersampling or oversampling. A run with the lever on therefore states 'No resampling ... or class weighting was applied' beside the lever's own sentence saying it was, and a user could copy that into a methods section. The default regime is right; only the scope of the sentence is wrong, so S2.

fix: In turbotab/core/materiality.py, keep rows_smd from ever predicting band 0 for an energy screen: set calibrated=false in materiality_calibration.json, since 9 in-sample cases from one fixture are too few. Reword recommend()'s band-0 text at materiality.py:1035-1037 ('below what would move the estimate'), and the band words, so they call the product an outcome-blind screening convention rather than a predictor of the movement. Make the every-row analysis the default verifier for any energy screen.
evidence: Both referees show that rows x max SMD on the adjustment set does not track the coefficient's movement. Adjusted-for covariate imbalance does not move a correctly specified coefficient; misreported exposure among the leavers does; and the proxy has no n. Referee A's simulation ranks the cases backwards. The repo's own calibration confirms this: the pairs are non-monotone, half the band-1 predictions (4/8) were realized at band 2 ('act on it'), and band_1 was refit in-sample to 0.0037. Yet the entry is marked calibrated:true. A narrow screen below 0.0037 is told 'That is below what would move the estimate', and the repo's own test documents a narrow screen at 0.019 that moved 0.63 half-widths. The 'checked again after the plan is fixed' promise holds only if an every-row analysis was declared, since realized_from_sensitivity returns None otherwise. That makes this a recommendation change in the reassuring direction.

fix: None needed; optionally add to the refusal at exposure_form.py:2140-2142 an exit 'to predict among consumers only, restrict who is studied (an eligibility rule on the exposure)'.
evidence: The code matches the claim. The refusal is at exposure_form.py:2138, the option is offered only under inference (:1101) with a recorded estimand-change sentence (:2069), and both referees and the audit accept the definitional part and the STROBE-nut nut-14 citation. Referee B objects that a consumers-only predictor for use among consumers is blocked. It is not: the refusal applies only to the exposure-form domain. A consumers-only population can be declared through the eligibility rules (set_exclusions accepts a range rule on a numeric exposure, decisions.py:3547), and then 'the model is used on everyone' in the declared population is exactly right.

fix: None now; when trials are wired (designs.py:56-61 NOT_YET), either refuse a declared non-inferiority/equivalence trial or add a hypothesis question so the 'itt' option text at trials.py:1879-1884 is scoped to superiority comparisons.
evidence: The ITT definition, its protection by randomization and its effect-of-assignment interpretation are correct and sourced (White et al. 2011; CONSORT 2010 E&E item 16, verified by the audit). The referees' missing-data caveat is already handled: an MAR primary on observed outcomes plus a delta tipping-point sensitivity analysis, disclosed in the notice. Their non-inferiority caveat does not bite on this app. The engine has no non-inferiority or equivalence analysis, and the per-protocol set is offered 'reported beside intention to treat, never instead', which is what the CONSORT NI extension asks for. Trial designs are also NOT_YET, so no user reaches this.

fix: In cox_fit (turbotab/core/models/survival.py:270-296), detect monotone likelihood without relying on |beta_z|>20. For example, flag a coefficient whose standardized value exceeds about 10 while its information eigenvalue collapses, or check each column for a level with no events in its risk sets, and refuse when pinv returns a zero or non-finite SE. Reword the parenthetical at :475-476 and :577-578 to 'a predictor orders the risk sets perfectly (for example, a group with no events)'. Add a test with a zero-event group plus one other covariate, and consider the Firth exit (Heinze & Schemper 2001).
evidence: Both referees are right that 'every row has the event' is not a Cox monotone-likelihood condition. In my run of the app's cox_fit, an all-event group interleaved with censored controls converges at beta*SD of -0.01. The worse problem is that the refusal misses the canonical monotone case. I ran cox_table with a binary group that has zero events plus one other covariate, 40 seeds per design at n=60-1000. It was refused in only 0-2 of 40 runs per design (1 at n=1000). Most runs instead reported a log HR of about -36 with SE about 1e-17, p = 0.0 and a zero-width 95% interval (26/40 at n=60). Others gave a Wald interval of plus or minus 1.5e7 with p=1.0, or no interval and no refusal. Newton's decrement falls below TOL=1e-18 at |beta_z| about 18, before the 20-SD trigger, and pinv zeroes the vanishing information. A user is shown a 'certain' infinite hazard ratio, with p = 0.0.

fix: In turbotab/core/estimand.py:183-185, treat the stored 'other' lens as no lens (return True when lens == ['other'] as well as when it is empty), as the comment at :176-178 states. Reword the skip at :207-209 to say this is a lens-based convention ('under this lens a yes/no outcome is usually a status at sampling ... if people were followed over time, Ask me anyway'). Add 'other' to test_routing_gate_repair's per-lens cases.
evidence: I ran follow_up_gate. Lens [] and ['clinical'] ask the question, while ['other'] ('Something else, or not sure', a stored Lens value, decisions.py:62) is skipped exactly like ['survey']. The code therefore contradicts its own rule that 'not sure' is always asked, and a 'not sure' cohort outcome is silently fit as one-period binary. Both referees are right that a missing follow-up-named column is absence of evidence and that assay or survey data can be incident events. The skip is soft ('Ask me anyway'), and with no time column a Cox model is unavailable anyway (Referee B's mitigation), so this is a scope and wording fix, not a wrong number in the main regime.

fix: In turbotab/core/readings.py:976-982, replace the fixed MINOR_SHARE floor with a direct test of the 'absent' reading: add ('none', 0.0) to _factor_alternatives (readings.py:937) so the loop at :984-990 rejects it from the observed ratio. Equivalently, use the floor 1 - ratio/PASS_HIGH, and reword the refusal so it no longer says any unit 'would hold as well' when that is not computed.
evidence: The ratio is declared/reconstructed (readings.py:983), so dropping a source raises it. Referee A's counterexamples (0.92 to 0.846, and 1.08 at 15% to 0.918) invert the ratio and are wrong. Referee B's point (the floor is 1 - R/1.10, exact only at R=1) is right. No wrong grams settlement follows: the kcal alternative removes 75-89% of a source's energy, so whenever it leaves the band the 'absent' reading does too. The only error is a needless refusal with a false reason when the median ratio exceeds 1. For example, at R=1.05 with an 8% share the 'absent' and kcal readings give 1.14 and 1.12, both out of band, yet the app says the identity 'would hold as well'. A refusal only waits for the user's recorded unit, and such low-share non-alcohol sources are rare, so S3. The audit's 'faithful/certified' is right for the main path.

fix: In turbotab/core/methods/omics.py:189-194, when the genomics lens sees a non-negative block that is non-integer, has a maximum of at least RAW_MAX and has widely varying row sums, raise the omics_scale question as 'ask: estimated counts or FPKM/TPM?' per GENOMICS_PACK.md §02 row 2, rather than returning None. Add genomics_estimated_counts.csv to test_the_reading_names_raw_values_and_stays_quiet_on_normalized_ones with the expected 'ask'.
evidence: I ran scale_reading under the genomics lens on the repo's own fixtures. genomics_estimated_counts.csv (non-integer, unnormalized, 'library sizes still vary widely', and marked 'ask' by its .md and by GENOMICS_PACK §02) returns None, the same as normalized CPM. Raw integer counts are read correctly. So salmon/kallisto/RSEM estimated counts, a common RNA-seq export, get no omics_scale finding, hence no normalization question and no linear-family refusal. That is the false negative both referees describe (non-integer counts fail the whole-number test), and it contradicts the repo's own pack. The cut-offs (100, 1,000, 0.5) are unsourced conventions, but the lognormal skew arithmetic checks out (Referees A and B).

fix: In turbotab/core/teaching/content.py:1018-1022, replace CLIN_A53 with the Nadeau & Bengio 2003 / Bouckaert & Frank 2004 citation. Reword the card to say the corrected repeated k-fold interval is approximate and usually conservative, and descriptive across several pairs (validation.py:581): one that excludes zero says a family is ahead, and one that includes zero says these rows cannot tell them apart, not that they are equal.
evidence: The card is tagged SETTLED and cites CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §A5.3, which is about discrimination versus calibration and does not support it (audit, accepted). I ran the app's corrected_t under a true null with 10x10 CV. The 'ahead' rate was 0.3% for OLS at n=40, 0-1% for exchangeable deep trees at n=30-40, and 0% at n=200. That supports Referee A's 'conservative' and does not reproduce Referee B's 8.7-12% for unstable learners. The verdict wording in family_differences ('not distinguishable on these rows') is fair, so the behavior is defensible. The card overstates what the interval 'tells' and carries a wrong source.

fix: Before P22 is built, amend docs/turbotab-next/calm/BEATS_PREDICT.md:1488 (§17 ruling 4). Give the reason for re-imputing in each fold as leakage: an unrecorded upstream fill may have used the outcome or other rows. Make the missing indicator conditional on whether the fill marker will exist at deployment and whether the original missingness is person-driven. Label the median-without-indicator choice a judgment, and add a test when P22 lands.
evidence: The audit's search confirms that no engine code serves this: P22 is listed as new work (BEATS_PREDICT.md:28, :1246), and the 'Read them as missing' beat was applied outside the engine. Both referees are right that the stated reason fails in realistic cases. Provider fills often stand in for person-level nonresponse, which can be informative, and if deployment data pass through the same pipeline the fill marker does exist at the moment of use. Sisk et al. 2023 found that indicators often help and do not support median fill. Re-imputing in each fold is sound for a different reason (leakage).

fix: In docs/turbotab-next/understanding/research/WHAT_EXPLORATION_MAY_DECIDE.md §1 (lines 11-21) and the prediction cell of the predictor-outcome row in §2, say that an outcome-informed candidate may enter only as a declared rule rerun in every fold, or else be scored only on the sealed hold-out. Label 'add, never prune' as the app's convention rather than a principle. Note that the registration-time enforcement (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §0 item 5) is not yet built.
evidence: Referees A and B disagree on whether add-only is safe, so I simulated it: n=60, 2,000 noise features, a declared search over 5, pure-noise outcome. Adding the top development-row correlate gave a CV MSE of 0.96 against a true MSE of 1.28. The declared search alone gave 1.14 against 1.13. Rerunning the same addition inside each fold gave 1.31, which is honest. Referee A is right that adding is as leaky as pruning. What protects the score is the doc's own §1 'rerun wherever the data are resampled' requirement or a sealed hold-out (Referee B's regime), and an eyeball addition cannot be rerun. The audit confirms no thread registry exists in turbotab/core, so the claimed refusal is unbuilt beyond specific validators.
